title: A sensor in the shade
bodyMd:
In a fictional workshop, two temperature sensors mounted on the same wall gave different readings each afternoon. One technician proposed replacing the higher-reading sensor. Another noticed that sunlight reached that sensor but not the other. When both were temporarily shielded from direct sun while remaining exposed to room air, their readings became much closer.

The team did not conclude that the instruments were perfectly accurate. Agreement between two sensors could still conceal a shared bias. However, the shielding test supported the idea that placement contributed to the original discrepancy. Future records included the mounting position and nearby heat sources, rather than treating each reading as a property of the instrument alone. A measurement was understood as the result of an instrument interacting with its environment under particular conditions.
